newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-ALL BLACKS OBLITERATE ARGENTINA.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-ALL BLACKS OBLITERATE ARGENTINA.

text.p: New Zealand, in a brilliant handling display, obliterated Argentina 93-8 in the first rugby test at Athletic Park on Saturday.
Playing in perfect weather, the All Blacks played rugby to match, displaying a huge gulf between the professional home side and the largely amateur Pumas.
With the sun and wind at their backs the All Blacks ran in seven first half tries and, proving their professionalism, did not let up, running in another seven in the second half.
The first try symbolically was initiated from a tighthead scrum followed by a line-out win from an Argentine throw-in.
It was scored by lock Ian Jones positioned in the three- quarter line, who had earlier won the line-out.
But it was the penultimate and last tries of the half in the 39th and 40th minutes that revealed the difference between the two sides.

Hometown wing Tana Umaga, starring in only his second test, having just waltzed through three tackles to score, was passed the ball from the kickoff near his own line, and proceeded to run through most of the Argentine team before unloading on the try-line to Josh Kronfeld to score.
Then, from the next kick-off, an action-replay was supplied by Christian Cullen, only he completed the entire 80 metre move himself.
The half-time break gave the Pumas no relief. With a 46-3 lead the All Blacks abandoned any pretence of caution.
Captain Sean Fitzpatrick, playing in his 85th test, completed one of the more memorable tries where virtually the entire team handled.
The Pumas finally scored a consolation try when from a ruck they went blindside and wing Tomas Solari got the overlap and cantered 50 metres to score.
But that was only a brief interruption to the onslaught. The All Blacks ran in a further five tries against the dispirited Pumas.
The All Blacks played with total arrogance. At one point number 8 Zinzan Brooke came to the Argentine 22, stopped, cross- kicked to the other side for his brother Robin Brooke to dot down.

Teams - All Blacks: 15-Christian Cullen (Glen Osborne); 14- Jeff Wilson, 13-Frank Bunce, 12-Lee Stensness, 11-Tana Umaga; 10-Carlos Spencer, 9-Justin Marshall; 8-Zinzan Brooke; 7-Josh Kronfeld, 6-Taine Randell, 5-Ian Jones, 4-Robin Brooke, 3-Olo Brown (Mark Allen), 2-Sean Fitzpatrick (captain), 1-Craig Dowd.

Argentina: 15-Ezequiel Jurado; 14-Tomas Solari, 13-Eduardo Simone, 12-Lisandro Arbizu (captain), 11-Facunda Soler; 10-Gonzalo Quesada, 9-Fernandez Miranda; 8-Pablo Camerlinckx; 7-Cristian Viel, 6-Rolando Martin, 5-Pedro Sporleder, 4-German Llanes; 3-Mauricio Reggiardo, 2-Carlos Promanzio, 1-Roberto Grau.
